title: "The Organizing Model"
subtitle: "ONTOLOGY blocks as organizing principles: field roles, production plan and SKOS export"

# The Organizing Model

The `ONTOLOGY` blocks of a Synesis project are its **organizing
principles**: the conceptual system through which the coded occurrences will
be understood. The compiler calls them together the **organizing model**, and
each block a **model entry**.

The name "ONTOLOGY" does not commit you to a formal ontology. The same
mechanism serves several degrees of organization, and the degree is a research
decision, not a format constraint:

| Degree | What the project declares | What it is for |
|---|---|---|
| **Flat list** | a name and a definition per concept | controlled vocabulary: `support_network` and `SupportNetwork` do not become two concepts |
| **Vocabulary with synonyms / thesaurus** | alternative and hidden labels, deprecated names | search and consolidation of variants |
| **Taxonomy** | "is a kind of" hierarchy | counts per subtree, navigation from general to specific |
| **Multi-relation taxonomy** | hierarchy with more than one species (kind, part, instance) and associative relations | SKOS publication, integration with other vocabularies |

No degree is called "ontology": SKOS is a **knowledge organization system**
(KOS) — vocabulary, thesaurus, taxonomy —, not a formal OWL ontology. The term
is reserved for an OWL export.

None of this needs special syntax in the `.syno`: these are ordinary template
fields (`SCOPE ONTOLOGY`) given a **function** with a `ROLE` line.

## The profile the compiler reports

At the end of `synesis compile`, the compiler describes what the project
declared — without judging whether the relations are valid:

```text
Structural Profile:
  Concepts:              19
  With definition:       19 (100%)
  Alternative labels:    8
  With KIND parent:      7
  With PART parent:      2
  Cycles:                none ✓
  Organizing model:      Terminological: With synonyms (1 code without concept)  |  Conceptual: Multi-relation taxonomy
  EXPORT SKOS:           Terminological: Thesaurus  |  Conceptual: Multi-relation taxonomy
```

The `Organizing model` line profiles the `.syno`; each `EXPORT SKOS` block
gets its own line, because an artifact may add relations (see
[MAP RELATIONS](#skos-export)). All ecosystem CLIs write their output in
English.

## Field roles: `ROLE`

A field's **type** gives the shape of its value; its `ROLE` line gives its
**function** in the organizing model. The field name stays free.

```synesis
FIELD definition TYPE TEXT
    SCOPE ONTOLOGY
    ROLE NOTE DEFINITION
END FIELD

FIELD used_for TYPE TEXT
    SCOPE ONTOLOGY
    ROLE LABEL ALTERNATIVE
END FIELD

FIELD kind_of TYPE CODE
    SCOPE ONTOLOGY
    ROLE HIERARCHY KIND
END FIELD
```

| Role | Type | Meaning | SKOS |
|---|---|---|---|
| `LABEL PREFERRED` | TEXT | display label (one per concept) | `skos:prefLabel` |
| `LABEL ALTERNATIVE` | TEXT | synonyms and variants | `skos:altLabel` |
| `LABEL HIDDEN` | TEXT | old or misspelled forms, for search only | `skos:hiddenLabel` |
| `NOTE DEFINITION` | TEXT | the concept's definition | `skos:definition` |
| `NOTE USAGE` | TEXT | when to apply the code | `skos:scopeNote` |
| `NOTE EXAMPLE` | TEXT | typical case | `skos:example` |
| `NOTE COUNTEREXAMPLE` | TEXT | similar case it does not apply to | `syn:counterExample` |
| `HIERARCHY KIND` | CODE | is a kind of | `skos:broader` |
| `HIERARCHY PART` | CODE | is part of | `skos:broader` |
| `HIERARCHY INSTANCE` | CODE | is an instance of | `skos:broader` |
| `USE` | CODE | deprecated name; use the concept given | label of the target |

With the function declared, the compiler validates the structure: a label
belongs to one concept only, the hierarchy points to the broader concept,
allows several parents and has no cycle. Each tool reads the field by its
role: the SKOS exporter, the `synesis-coder` phases, `synesis-graph`
(`KIND_OF`, `PART_OF`, `INSTANCE_OF` edges) and the LSP (hover with parents
and children).

```synesis
ONTOLOGY smishing
    definition: Phishing carried out through SMS messages.
    used_for: SMS phishing
    kind_of: phishing
END ONTOLOGY
```

### What sources state and what the project adopts

The hierarchy in the `.syno` is what the **project adopts**. What the
**sources state** stays in the annotations' chains (`CHAIN`), with evidence.
The two do not mix: a chain `smishing -> KIND_OF -> phishing` puts nothing in
the `.syno`. To bring it into an artifact, use `MAP RELATIONS` in the
[EXPORT block](#skos-export).

### Merging two names: `USE`

When two blocks name the same concept, the deprecated one keeps only the
`USE`-role field:

```synesis
ONTOLOGY voice_phishing
    use: vishing
END ONTOLOGY
```

Annotations do not change. Counts, hierarchy, graph and SKOS add the
deprecated block to its target, and the deprecated name becomes a label of the
target. `synesis-coder consolidate project.synp voice_phishing --into vishing`
makes the edit with a manifest; `--revert` undoes it.

## Competency questions: `QUESTIONS`

The `.synp` can declare what the project must be able to answer:

```synesis
QUESTIONS
    Q1: Which evidence concerns phishing or any of its subtypes?
    Q2: Which concepts have no direct or indirect evidence?
END QUESTIONS
```

The questions guide the template design and serve as acceptance criteria for
the organizing model. They appear in the compiled JSON, in the graph context
and in the project context `synesis-coder` sends to the model.

## Production plan: `PHASE`

`PHASE` blocks split the production of the organizing model into phases, each
with its own fields:

```synesis
PHASE ONTOLOGY definitions
    FIELDS definition, topic
    INPUT excerpt, chain
END PHASE

PHASE ONTOLOGY synonyms
    FIELDS used_for, hidden_label
    INPUT definition, topic
END PHASE

PHASE ONTOLOGY taxonomy
    FIELDS kind_of, part_of
    INPUT definition, topic, chain
END PHASE
```

The compiler validates the plan against the template (existing fields, phase
order, required fields covered). Each phase's kind comes from the roles:
`HIERARCHY` fields make a taxonomy phase, `LABEL ALTERNATIVE` or `HIDDEN`
fields a synonyms phase, and the rest a descriptive phase.

```bash
synesis-coder phase project.synp --list          # the plan and each phase's connection
synesis-coder phase project.synp definitions     # run one phase
synesis-coder review project.synp taxonomy --sample 100
synesis-coder review project.synp taxonomy --score sample.csv
```

Each run writes a manifest (`<destination>.<phase>.manifest.json`) recording
what was proposed, applied or rejected; running again with unchanged inputs
does not call the model. `review` draws a stratified sample for human
judgement and estimates precision with inclusion weights. Model and connection
can differ per phase (`SYNESIS_CODER_PHASE_<NAME>_MODEL`, `_BACKEND`,
`_API_URL`, `_API_KEY`).

## SKOS export

A project's artifacts are declared in `EXPORT` blocks of the `.synp` and run
with `synesis export project.synp`. The `SKOS` format publishes the organizing
model as a SKOS vocabulary (a KOS) in Turtle:

```synesis
EXPORT SKOS corroborated
    OUTPUT "out/fraud.ttl"
    NAMESPACE "https://example.org/id/fraud/"
    LANGUAGE en
    MIN_SOURCES 2
    MAP RELATIONS KIND_OF TO HIERARCHY KIND
    MAP RELATIONS MITIGATES, EXPLOITS TO RELATED
END EXPORT
```

- **`MAP RELATIONS`** brings chain relations into a role (`HIERARCHY KIND`,
  `PART`, `INSTANCE` or `RELATED`) **in this artifact only**. The `.syno`,
  dashboards and graph do not see the mapping.
- **`MIN_SOURCES`** is the minimum number of distinct sources stating a pair
  for it to enter the file. Two blocks with different thresholds separate the
  corroborated pairs from the candidates.
- **`ALIAS_LABEL HIDDEN|ALTERNATIVE`** decides how a deprecated name (`USE`)
  enters its target; the default is `HIDDEN`.
- **`REGISTRY "<file>"`** with `synesis export --publish` records the
  published IRIs. If a published concept is later deprecated, its old IRI is
  exported as obsolete (`owl:deprecated`, `dcterms:isReplacedBy`) instead of
  disappearing.

### IRI policy

Each concept gets the IRI `NAMESPACE` + `concept/` + block name. The
`NAMESPACE` belongs to the **project**: a domain the team controls and keeps,
ending in `/` or `#`. `example.org` is for testing, never for publication.
Because the IRI derives from the name, renaming a concept changes its IRI:
after publishing, use `USE` with `REGISTRY` so the old IRI keeps resolving to
the new one.

The `NAMESPACE` is the researcher's decision: changing it blocks neither the
export nor the publication. If the `REGISTRY` holds IRIs from another
namespace, `synesis export` warns how many were left out of the check
(`SYNESIS_E156`) — links to them break unless the old address redirects. With
`--publish`, an unreadable `REGISTRY` is an error (nothing is written), and
`OUTPUT` and `REGISTRY` on the same file are always refused (`SYNESIS_E157`).

### The `syn:` vocabulary

SKOS covers almost everything. The two missing terms are in the
[`syn:`](https://synesis-lang.org/ns/syn/) vocabulary
(`https://synesis-lang.org/ns/syn#`, file
[`syn.ttl`](https://synesis-lang.org/ns/syn.ttl)):

- `syn:counterExample`, subproperty of `skos:note`, for `NOTE COUNTEREXAMPLE`;
- `syn:classifiedBy`, superproperty of the properties generated for
  `ENUMERATED` and `ORDERED` fields, whose values become `skos:ConceptScheme`.
